title: fix(cron): preserve Gateway plugin registry for scheduled runs
body:
Fixes #166756

## What Problem This Solves

The first scheduled condition check after Gateway restart can synchronously reload plugins already loaded at startup, exhaust its 30-second budget, and stall Gateway liveness and channel sockets.

## User Impact

Scheduled condition checks reuse their Gateway's current compatible plugins after restart and cron hot reload. The existing trigger deadline, tool policy, request isolation, and plugin-generation checks are preserved. No configuration, protocol, SDK, schema, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Detached scheduling deliberately drops request-local state. The cron owner now supplies a live registry resolver through startup, lazy construction, and hot reload, allowing preparation to use the existing Gateway-owned borrowing path. Resolving it per run follows registry replacement without borrowing another Gateway's resources.

Maintainer cleanup removes the ambient request-registry fallback, shares the cron constructor's parameter contract with its lazy adapter, and replaces helper-identity/constructor-argument assertions with real preparation, tool execution, registration-count, and generation coverage.

Original fix by @67-luck; maintainer cleanup and proof by @steipete. Contributor commits and human co-author credit are preserved.

## Evidence

Verified candidate `c36968226bded0675e8ef07b5adaae9dc4781b31` against captured main `57dd17b4ea39b5f5d87db9faabaa2f0b10fa83f4`. [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37790171051). Independent Codex autoreview was scoped-clean through P2. This PR is intentionally left unmerged.

Real Gateway proof ran on secretless AWS lease `cbx_211600b2dc4e` (`r7i.xlarge`, 30.81 GiB RAM), with the QA mock OpenAI provider, isolated state, and ephemeral ports. The fixture loaded 31 local plugins with calibrated synchronous PBKDF2 work in `register`, making duplicate registration measurable without patching production code. These are synthetic registration costs, not a benchmark of the reporter's plugin fleet. Evaluations were naturally scheduled; forced runs, which bypass the condition, were not used. The first evaluation followed a full process restart and the 60-second liveness startup grace.

| Revision / first evaluation | Completion after due | Additional plugin registrations | Observed result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Main, after process restart | 35,585 ms | 31 (35,195 ms registration CPU) | Trigger timeout; liveness 20,235 ms overdue; 20 health timeouts |
| Main, after cron hot reload | 30,354 ms after advertised due | 0 | Quiet check persisted generation 1 from warm cache; no new liveness warning or health timeout |
| Fix, after process restart | 306 ms | 0 | Condition state persisted; no liveness warning or health timeout |
| Fix, after cron hot reload | 201 ms | 0 | Same Gateway PID; condition state persisted; no liveness warning or health timeout |
| Fix, after plugin generation replacement and cron hot reload | 167 ms | 0 | Returned generation 2; no liveness warning or health timeout |
| Fix, condition-fired agent turn | 4,307 ms (4,170 ms payload run) | 0 | One mock-provider request; one successful persisted run; `REGISTRY_OK` |

After main's initial timeout, the warm-cache reload observation completed without another registry load. Its 30,354 ms figure is completion after the advertised due time, not a measured CPU stall. Quiet conditions preserve prior payload-run status, so the retained `error` was not counted as a second timeout.

Cron replacement was exercised through supported `config.patch` updates of `cron.enabled` false then true. The Gateway PID remained unchanged. `plugins.reload` deliberately re-registered only the selected probe plugin once; the subsequent condition borrowed that new generation without registering it again.

Main evidence:

```text
cron trigger evaluation failed (timeout): cron trigger evaluation timed out
liveness heartbeat delayed: overdue=20235ms elapsed=50235ms; deferring recovery decisions
```

All 283 tests across the 19 trigger/cron/Gateway module files passed (156.92 s wall). The changed preparation file passed 5 tests with `pnpm test src/cron/trigger-script.preparation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (58.93 s cold wall, mostly worker compilation); the new regression took 879 ms within the module run. CI's 17 Node validation jobs totaled 3,856 runner-seconds, including setup and existing selected coverage, not just the added regression.

The production-only negative control kept the test unchanged and reverted only `scheduled-run-gateway-context.ts` to the main merge-base version. It failed on the intended assertion: startup's single `full` registration was followed by unwanted `discovery` and `tool-discovery` registrations. The fixed production file was restored byte-for-byte before subsequent checks.

Production typecheck passed (63.06 s), as did the three applicable test-type graphs (166.44 s combined). Full build with QA artifacts passed (382.88 s). Local oxfmt, scoped oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed; no contributor runtime executed locally. The full build reported an unrelated UI startup-bundle-size warning; UI source is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Commands and source isolation</summary>

The installed Crabbox CLI was launched from a clean trusted main worktree. Every run used the trusted bootstrap, the full pushed PR SHA, `--fresh-pr`, `--no-hydrate`, and `CRABBOX_ENV_ALLOW=CI`. The bootstrap verified the SHA and IMDS no-role boundary and installed dependencies in a fresh temporary HOME. Public networking and no Tailscale were verified before use.

```sh
env -u CRABBOX_AWS_INSTANCE_PROFILE CRABBOX_ENV_ALLOW=CI \
  crabbox run --provider aws --id cbx_211600b2dc4e \
  --fresh-pr openclaw/openclaw#166991 --no-hydrate --timing-json \
  --script scripts/crabbox-untrusted-bootstrap.sh -- \
  c36968226bded0675e8ef07b5adaae9dc4781b31 bash -c '<scoped check commands>'

pnpm test src/cron/trigger-script.preparation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test src/cron/trigger-script*.test.ts src/gateway/server-cron*.test.ts \
  src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-reload-hot.cron-lazy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm tsgo:core:test --ci-graphs-json \
  '["core-test-services-cron","core-test-gateway-server","core-test-gateway-root"]'
OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build

# Temporary real-Gateway harness; same input fixture on each revision.
pnpm exec tsx /tmp/166991-live-proof.mts --repo-root "$PWD" \
  --head c36968226bded0675e8ef07b5adaae9dc4781b31 --expect fixed \
  --output-dir /tmp/oc-r6-166991-proof/fixed-live-corrected
pnpm exec tsx /tmp/166991-live-proof.mts --repo-root "$PWD" \
  --head c36968226bded0675e8ef07b5adaae9dc4781b31 --expect fixed --turn-only \
  --output-dir /tmp/oc-r6-166991-proof/fixed-live-turn

# Separate remote main worktree; native runtime build for the baseline.
git fetch --no-tags https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git \
  57dd17b4ea39b5f5d87db9faabaa2f0b10fa83f4 --depth=1
git worktree add --detach /tmp/oc-r6-166991-main \
  57dd17b4ea39b5f5d87db9faabaa2f0b10fa83f4
cd /tmp/oc-r6-166991-main
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build qaRuntime
pnpm exec tsx /tmp/166991-live-proof.mts --repo-root "$PWD" \
  --head 57dd17b4ea39b5f5d87db9faabaa2f0b10fa83f4 --expect baseline \
  --output-dir /tmp/oc-r6-166991-proof/main-live
```

The original-head baseline also passed 32 tests on lease `cbx_b35b1f297781`. An allocation that fell back to `t3.small` (`cbx_a77651d52052`) was stopped without executing candidate code; the memory-capable replacement supplied the final proof.

Two temporary-harness issues were corrected without changing product code: a retired `cron.maxConcurrentRuns` option, and a counter comparison made before replacing the trigger definition (the owner correctly resets that counter). The three passing registry phases were retained; the fired-turn observation was rerun and passed. After the full build gate passed, `pnpm build qaRuntime` supplied runtime artifacts for the remaining harness-only work. No failing product check was hidden by a retry.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Review findings and exact change size</summary>

The latest ClawSweeper review had no production-code finding. Its missing real restart/hot-reload evidence is supplied above. Both low-value plumbing assertions were removed and replaced with the preparation regression and production-only negative control. No human review findings were outstanding.

Against main's PR merge base: production +25 / -26 (net -1); tests +86 / -4 (net +82); docs +0 / -0. Existing schedule documentation already specifies the behavior restored by this fix. No changelog edits.
